Regarding the definition of "zero-shot generalization" in the context of text-to-image AIs, it seems sensible. The concept of zero-shot generalization refers to the ability of a model to apply its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts without requiring additional training data. In the context of text-to-image AIs, this means that the model can generate images based on text prompts without having seen the specific images or concepts before.

The 2013 paper that the paper cites likely discussed the concept of zero-shot generalization in the context of deep learning and neural networks, where it refers to the ability of a model to generalize to new, unseen data without requiring additional training. For example, if a text-to-image AI is trained on a dataset of images of cats and dogs, it may be able to generate images of other animals, such as birds or fish, without having seen them before. This is an example of zero-shot generalization, as the model is applying its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts.
